A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dataset Distillation via the Wasserstein Metric. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original WMDD classification results, cross-architecture experiments, ablations, synthetic-image analyses, and resource measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and additionally reports a controlled MMD comparison and comparative efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The reported barycenter solver changes: v1 Appendix A uses accelerated KL-Bregman weight updates and optionally damped Newton steps; v2 Appendix D specifies projected subgradient weight updates and fixed-iteration Newton updates. The feature-space barycenter matching and per-class BatchNorm loss remain unchanged. These are changes to the specified procedure, without establishing which implementation produced retained results.

E1.justification: ImageNette, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-1K classification coverage remains unchanged. The limited scenario change is Figure 1's toy simulation: v1 uses circle-supported distributions, whereas v2 includes circles and crosses. The additional MMD and efficiency experiments use existing image datasets.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds CDA and removes the separate replicated SRe2L comparisons for Tiny-ImageNet and ImageNet-1K, retaining published SRe2L results. The previously WMDD-only efficiency comparison expands to DC, DM, and SRe2L in Table 6. Table 4 also introduces a dedicated comparison against the already represented DM method under controlled settings.

E3.justification: New Section 5.5 compares metrics without FKD or elaborate augmentations, retaining random cropping and horizontal flipping for student training. Efficiency evaluation changes from V100 at 64×64 resolution to RTX-3090 at original resolution, with a common 2,000-iteration budget and revised timing definition. Tiny-ImageNet's reported regularization coefficient changes from 500 to 300; the PDFs do not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a controlled investigation of Wasserstein versus MMD performance and expands resource reporting into comparative efficiency analysis. It removes the visual barycenter-loss on/off comparison from v1 Figure 9, while retaining the numerical component ablation. Cross-architecture testing, regularization sensitivity, and feature-distribution analyses largely persist.

E5.justification: Both versions report classification means across three runs. v2 adds uncertainty to the previously unqualified ImageNette 100-IPC entries: WMDD 87.1±0.3 and replicated SRe2L 85.9±0.2. Table 6 newly reports timing means and standard deviations over 100 consecutive iterations, not 100 independent experiment runs.

E6.justification: WMDD's headline accuracy means, cross-architecture scores, and numerical ablations are retained. v2 adds CDA results and Table 4's Wasserstein accuracies of 5.77/10.45/20.41 versus MMD's 0.48/9.03/19.10 at 1/10/50 IPC. It replaces efficiency results under different conditions and omits replicated SRe2L results at 1, 50, and 100 IPC on Tiny-ImageNet and ImageNet; the 10-IPC baseline scores remain in the ablation table.

T1.justification: The Wasserstein definitions, transport primal-dual formulation, and basic alternating optimization already appear in v1. v2 adds explicit gradient and Hessian derivations and a conditional convergence statement for projected subgradient updates, while removing v1's KL-Bregman proximal construction. Naming the existing distribution-matching premise Assumption A1 does not itself introduce a new assumption.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a novel Wasserstein-barycenter approach to feature-space dataset distillation that preserves distribution-matching efficiency and achieves strong or state-of-the-art high-resolution benchmark performance. Rewritten contributions and conclusions retain this scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 newly attributes poor low-IPC MMD performance to empirical approximation and emphasis on feature means. Appendices A–B discuss inherited dataset biases, computational overhead, and dependence on a source-domain pretrained classifier, proposing self-supervised or generative extensions. Existing interpretations of generalization and synthetic-image diversity largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 Table 5a newly specifies pretraining details including SGD, momentum 0.9, weight decay 1e-4, cosine scheduling, and 100 epochs. v2 adds code-release-upon-acceptance and accompanying-ZIP statements, but neither PDF embeds that code. It removes v1's approximately 14-hour ImageNet/A40 run estimate and revises the documented Tiny-ImageNet regularization value.

R1.justification: The SRe2L-focused related-work subsection becomes a broader distribution-matching discussion, incorporating works such as IDM, M3D, and Sun et al.; CDA is also newly cited and compared. Several alternative Wasserstein-solver and accelerated-optimization references disappear. The central positioning at the intersection of distribution matching and optimal transport remains.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, and conclusion; separates preliminary material from the method; reorganizes computation explanations; and restructures the supplementary material into Appendices A–G. Author information and citation style also change. This exceeds simple renumbering or the insertion of new experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one, with extensive table resizing and figure rearrangement. v1's separate sensitivity plot and image panel become v2 Figure 2, and the t-SNE panels become horizontal. Image galleries are consolidated, Hay and Flamingo comparisons exchange main-text/appendix placement, Figure 1 is redrawn, and new comparison tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful controlled comparisons, training details, mathematical derivations, and explicit limitations. However, it removes stronger replicated SRe2L results from the main comparison, including Tiny-ImageNet's 59.8% at 100 IPC versus WMDD's 61.0%, weakening assessment of the claimed advantage. Retained accuracy means also accompany changed optimizer descriptions and regularization settings without reconciliation. These gains and losses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
